name: Habsburg Monarchy (Leopold I)

areaKm2.note: world_1700 "Austrian Empire" polygons = 426,621 km2 on the sphere but cover mainly Hungary, Croatia and Transylvania; the hereditary lands, Bohemia, Moravia and Silesia (~200,000 km2) lie inside the Holy Roman Empire polygon of that file and are not drawn. Sum ~600,000 km2. The map border therefore understates the monarchy.

population.note: HYDE via OWID (1700, modern borders): Austria 2.12M, Czechia 3.24M, Hungary 1.50M, Slovakia 1.14M, Croatia 0.66M, Slovenia 0.25M, plus Silesia (~1.0M), Transylvania (~0.8M) and South Tyrol/Trentino (~0.2M) = ~10.9M. The Military Revolution article gives 8M for c. 1650 (before the reconquest of Hungary). Mid 10.5M. Spanish Netherlands and Milan (1714) excluded.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share: Austria 4.8%, Czechia 4.8%, Hungary 4.8% (1700, de Vries-type). Mid 5%.

activePersonnel.note: Kaiserliche Armee (the Habsburg standing army) averaged ~70,000 in the Great Turkish War (1683-89) and the Nine Years War (Wilson 2016 via the Imperial Army of the Holy Roman Emperor article); Parker gives 110,000-130,000 for c. 1700-10 (Military Revolution article) and 20,000-24,000 for the 1650s. After Karlowitz (1699) regiments were reduced; mid ~80,000 incl. Danube flotilla and artillery. Reichsarmee contingents of the Empire excluded.

trainedReserves.note: Military Frontier border militia (Grenzer, ~20,000-40,000 able to serve), the Hungarian noble insurrectio and Bohemian/Austrian Landesdefension levies. Hochedlinger, Austria's Wars of Emergence (isbn:0-582-29084-8), ch. 6, describes the Grenzer as a part-time militia.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess: artillery (Feldzeugamt), pontoniers and Danube flotilla (Tschaikisten), staff and commissariat.

mobilizationRatio.note: Peaks of 110,000-130,000 regulars (Military Revolution article, Parker) plus Grenzer on ~10.5M = 1.5-2%; ceiling ~3-4% with insurrectio levies.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: German infantry regiments (~2/3 of the Kaiserliche Armee).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical) to 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: flintlock and bayonet adopted in the 1690s, some pikes retained

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: veterans of 16 years of war against the Ottomans (Zenta 1697)

count.note: Cuirassier regiments, the core of the Habsburg cavalry.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: heavy cuirassiers, among the best battle cavalry

count.note: Dragoon regiments and Hungarian hussars (counted as light cavalry).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: hussars the model for Europe's light cavalry

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: frontier warfare experience

count.note: Educated guess: field pieces of the Feldzeugamt; Eugene took ~60-80 guns on campaign.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: artillery the weakest Habsburg arm before Liechtenstein's reforms (1744)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: guild-like civilian gunners

count.note: Educated guess: Danube flotilla of armed boats (tschaiken) and a few Adriatic vessels; no seagoing navy.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: river craft

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: Tschaikisten border militia

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Eugene of Savoy (Zenta 1697) and Ludwig of Baden; Hofkriegsrat slow and underfunded

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: standing regiments owned by Inhaber colonels; multinational

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75. Evidence: reconquest of Hungary 1683-99, Zenta (1697), Karlowitz (1699)

weapons.note: Anchor: 5.5 between 1600 and 1805. Evidence: flintlock and socket bayonet in the 1690s

ships.note: Anchor: 4.5. Evidence: river flotilla only; no ocean navy

fortification.note: Anchor: 5.6. Evidence: bastioned fortresses at Komarom, Gyor, Petrovaradin (rebuilt from 1692) audit 2026-10-30: mid 5.6 -> 5.49, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1700 (5.488); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

logistics.note: Anchor: 5.1. Evidence: Danube shipping and magazines for Hungarian campaigns

communications.note: Anchor: 5.0. Evidence: imperial post (Paar) courier network

isr.note: Anchor: ISR uses the same years as the anchor table (1600 -> 5, 1805 -> 6). Evidence: cavalry screens, spies and merchant reports only; no aerial or signal intelligence

air.note: No aircraft or military balloons before 1783/1794.

gdpPerCapita.note: Analogue: Germany 1700 = 1,511 (Maddison Project 2023, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) scaled by the Austria/Germany ratio in 1820 (1,941/2,041 = 0.95, MPD 2020, https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/historicaldevelopment/maddison/data/mpd2020.xlsx) = ~1,440 for the hereditary lands and Bohemia; Hungary, war-ravaged after 1683-99, lower. Mid 1,300. No Maddison series for Austria or Hungary before 1820.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: state revenue ~12-15M florins dominated by army costs; war loans from Oppenheimer; peacetime 1700.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: Bohemian and Silesian linen and glass, Styrian iron; Hungary pastoral.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: Hungarian plain under-populated but fertile; Bohemia self-sufficient.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.009-0.011 (mid 0.0095): in a pre-transition age structure (Wrigley and Schofield type, life expectancy ~30-35) males reaching 18 each year are about 0.9-1.1% of total population. Males only.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: post roads Vienna-Prague-Breslau and Vienna-Graz-Trieste; Danube the main military artery.

majorPorts.note: Trieste and Fiume (minor Adriatic ports); Danube river ports (Vienna, Pressburg, Buda) for military supply.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: negligible seagoing merchant fleet; Danube barges not counted.

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War (isbn:0-521-54657-5) ch. 1: 17th-18th c. armies tied to magazines and bread ovens, operating ~5 marches (~100-150 km) beyond the nearest magazine or navigable river; requisition extends it in rich country. Hungarian campaigns followed the Danube. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: Hungarian horse and cattle herds, Bohemian draught animals.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: fortified Danube line, Alps and Bohemian hills; Hungary restive (Rakoczi revolt 1703).

notes: Snapshot = 1700, after the Peace of Karlowitz (1699) and before the War of the Spanish Succession. Population: hereditary lands, Bohemian crown lands (incl. Silesia) and Hungary with Croatia and Transylvania; the Spanish inheritance (1714) and Reich contingents excluded. Personnel convention: the Kaiserliche Armee regiments are active; Grenzer, Hungarian insurrectio and Landesdefension levies are trainedReserves. The map border (world_1700 "Austrian Empire") draws only the Hungarian lands; the core lands sit in that file's Holy Roman Empire polygon, so the rendered area understates the monarchy. Habsburg army size in 1700 is uncertain (post-war reductions); range 60,000-100,000.
